Livestock manure, like cow dung in the absence of appropriate disposal methods can cause adverse environmental and health problems such as: pathogen contamination, odour, air borne ammonia, green house gases, etc. In this work, the utilization of biomass (cow dung) to produce biogas through anaerobic digestion for power generation is presented. The experiment was batch operated and was kept for 30 days. The enhancement technique for biogas generation is done through agitation process powered by a 12Volt, 750mAh UPS battery charged from a 5 Watt solar panel. The biogas composition is analysed using a Gas Chromatography. For power generation, the biogas was used for heating water through a normal LPG burner and the steam produced is used for running a turbine coupled with a 12volt DC generator.

articleTitle: Design and development of permanent magnet induction generator for renewable energy applications: A review
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Innovations in Electrical, Electronics, Instrumentation and Media Technology (ICEEIMT)
abstract: Renewable energy and all sources of non-conventional energy are catching an eye in the field of power generation. Modern technologies, research and innovations are done for optimization of those power harvesting techniques which focus on reducing the cost and increasing the efficiency of the available means. The induction generator is the vital component of power generation network. This paper present the review of design and developmental aspects of permanent magnet induction generator utilized for renewable energy applications. The constructional details including the magnetic properties of materials used for manufacturing permanent magnet induction generator is also highlighted in this paper. The paper also discusses various real-time applications of induction generator in detail. The paper depicts an overview of permanent magnet induction generator and its various fields of applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid optimization algorithms for analyzing the performance of transmission system incorporating advanced SVC model
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Innovations in Electrical, Electronics, Instrumentation and Media Technology (ICEEIMT)
abstract: The multiplicity of transactions frequently leads to the conditions where the operating zone will not remain secure in the field of emerging electric power systems. In the system of power security advancement, the highly Flexible AC transmission systems (FACTs) controllers will play a prime role. But because of large scale capital investment it is required to locate the FACTs controllers in the power system in optimum condition. Due to the flexibility nature of these controllers, with fast control characteristics they may regulate both active and reactive power flow control cum adaptive to voltage magnitude control very effectively. Regulation in line flow and maintenance of voltages at different locations of the bus are achieved by keeping of such devices in suitable location. In this paper optimization methods GA-PSO and DA-PSO are proposed for finding the optimum location and firing angle of SVC. In that, the location of the device is optimized by GA or DA and the optimized firing angle is done with PSO. Because of the two different Optimizing techniques are used to solve single objective function, it is called Hybridization. The proposed optimization is an effective method for finding the optimal location of SVC device and also increasing voltage profile and reducing the power system losses in the line. This Hybrid GA-PSO and DA-PSO is tested on IEEE 57 bus test systems and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: An effective methodology for short-term generation scheduling of hydrothermal power system using improved TLBO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Innovations in Electrical, Electronics, Instrumentation and Media Technology (ICEEIMT)
abstract: The Short-Term Hydrothermal Scheduling (STHTS) is one of the most prominent exercise in the field of power system. It advocates the scheduling of hydro and thermal generations so as to minimize the fuel cost over the planning period by satisfying standard system constraints. The problem of scheduling of a generation mixture of thermal and hydro problems are modelled as a non linear, non convex problems comprising valve point loading effects and a set of equality and inequality constraints. The interpretation of hydrothermal systems with hydro predominance is significantly more complex than hydro system. This problem is extremely difficult to deal using classical techniques. This paper presents a simple and novel concept of improved Teaching Learning based Optimization (ITLBO) algorithm for the solution of short term hydro thermal scheduling problem. The TLBO algorithm is an exceptional distinct optimization algorithm stimulated by the effect of influence of a teacher on the productivity of learners in the domain. The proposed methodology has been applied on a standard test system consisting of four hydro an equivalent thermal unit for 24 hours. The results are evolved in terms of water discharge, reservoir storage volume and fuel cost of thermal units with/without valve point loading effects. The performance of the proposed method is validated by comparing with other methods available in the literature. From the findings, it is obvious that ITLBO based approach is able to provide a better solution.
